note: SKILL.md loads the two exemplars matching the document type at write time. status_update is empty: no public exemplar family exists for it in either split, so that genre tests whether the rules transfer without an exemplar to imitate.

design_doc.why: Mechanism carried almost entirely without numbers: 0.22 numbers per 100 words, mechanism:evaluative 3.00, and 0.7% of sentences over 30 words. The counter-example to the idea that good technical prose is dense with figures.
One idea, built from a worked combinatorial example the reader can redo. 1,773 words, claim-first 0.895.
Argues a policy position from quantities without becoming a spreadsheet. Claim-first 0.878, hedges 1.39 per 100 words, all of them load-bearing.

rfc.why: A proposal that spends most of its length on the objections to itself. Mechanism:evaluative 4.00, claim-first 0.917.
879 words for a language change. Mechanism:evaluative 7.00. The shortest thing in the corpus that fully carries a design decision.

postmortem.why: Claim-first 0.950 and 3.32 numbers per 100 words with mechanism:evaluative 5.20 - the combination the other incident reports miss, because most of them narrate status without ever saying why.
Mechanism:evaluative 7.40, the highest in the corpus. Reads postmortems against each other rather than summarising them.
Claim-first 1.000 across 22 paragraphs, 8.6% of sentences over 30 words. The cleanest paragraph discipline measured.

perf_analysis.why: 50% of sentences run over 30 words and it is still easy to read, because each long sentence resolves clause by clause. The document that refutes a sentence-length cap.
Sustains an argument over 4,818 words on one carried example. Mechanism:evaluative 2.60, hedges 2.18 per 100 words.
